newsitem.title: GERMANY: German poll puts opposition ahead of Kohl alliance.
newsitem.headline: German poll puts opposition ahead of Kohl alliance.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition would lose its majority if an election were held this weekend, according to an opinion poll for Germany's ZDF television released on Friday.

The monthly Politbarometer survey said Kohl's coalition of Christian Democrats and Free Democrats would win 45 percent of the vote while the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and the Greens, their most likely partners, would together win 47 percent.

Last month's Politbarometer had Kohl's alliance ahead with 47 percent compared to 45 percent for an SPD-Green coalition, but most other polls over the last few months have indicated a majority for the opposition.

The next general election is due in October 1998. The Electoral Research Group carried out telephone interviews with 1,251 Germans for the latest ZDF poll, which has a margin of error of 2.5 percent for larger parties and around 1.5 for smaller ones.
Kohl has not yet said if he will run for re-election in 1998. ZDF said that for the first time in his current term, a majority of respondents -- 56 percent -- believed he should not stand again.
The SPD has not yet chosen its candidate to challenge for the chancellor's job.
Echoing a finding of several other recent polls, the survey found Gerhard Schroeder, the SPD premier of Lower Saxony state, would be the SPD's best candidate.
In a direct comparison of the two, 46 percent of respondents said they would prefer Schroeder while 40 percent favoured Kohl.
Voters still preferred Kohl as chancellor to SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine, but the gap between them narrowed to six percentage points from 14 in January, ZDF said.
